steps.why: The words successive trophic level are the definition: the pollutant does not simply build up in one animal, it becomes more concentrated at every step UP the chain.
common_mistakes: Writing that the pollutant increases in the water. It increases in the ORGANISMS along the chain.
Leaving out the reason. The pollutant builds up because the body cannot break it down.
steps.memory_tip: Each level eats many of the level below, so the poison of many bodies ends up in one.
steps.margin_note: One sentence for the increase, one for the reason. Use the words trophic level.

steps.why: The two numbers make the word magnification concrete, and the jump from parts per billion to parts per million is the single fact that shows how large the increase is.
common_mistakes: Giving the numbers without their units. ppb and ppm are what make the jump visible.
Naming a gas such as carbon dioxide. The standard example is DDT in a water food chain.
steps.memory_tip: 0.003 ppb in the water, 5 ppm in the birds: billion becomes million on the way up.
steps.margin_note: Name DDT and give both numbers with their units. Four lines are enough.

insider_note: The two DDT numbers are what the examiner is looking for, and they must carry their units — ppb in the water and ppm in the birds.
